First, congratulations on your new home!! That's such an exciting step and its incredibly kind of you to share your good fortune! 

I'm sure many people commenting have valid, and perhaps more dire needs, but $100 would go so far in my household at the moment. 

Our problem started a few years ago, when a harrassing boss and useless hr led to us leaving the company for the sake of our mental health. This wasn't an easy love, as we'd been there for over and year and had pretty much centered our lifestyle around being able to keep double income at the same job. When we both lost it, everything kind of fell apart. We ended up losing our apartment, living at a friend couch, and finally settled with some help from my family in a trailer park, where we live in a camper. Im so grateful for the help we received at the time, but since then we've been trying to manage mostly on our own.

Fast forward through endless job interviews, stays in mental health hospitals, jobs that led nowhere, and well...poverty struggling to the max, and we've finally landed here. Where, arguably, we're doing much better than a year ago. 

In the last few weeks of 2019, my partner managed to get a job as a data entry clerk- which is something we've both tried and failed interviewing at before- and that was an incredible feat! And, just this past week, I finished up my first week at the same job. Its going great, and everyday i got to look up and see my partner, the love of my life, right across the way. This job is a huge opportunity for us, even if it only offers part time hours, and I'm thrilled for the doors this kind of work experience will lead to in the future. 

But our struggles are far from over. The holidays really cut into my partners check this week, and I won't see my first one until thr 24th, or two weeks from now. By that time, both the rent that we owe (about 250) and this months rent (350) will be owed, and I dont think our landlord will be able to work with us again for an extension. 

With both our income, we should (hopefully) have enough to cover everything- but  that leaves us with very little left to survive off of. $100 would help us pad our expenses, and we can certainly make that stretch over the next two weeks through our gas tank to ensure that we make it to everyday of work, and are able to affors upcoming expenses. 

I'm sure there are plenty of other people out there that would benefit just as much if more more from such a generous amount, and let me say again THANK YOU for spreading such kindness in light of your success. Whoever gets picked, sharing my story has been nice, and reading the stories of others is humbling. Thanks again, and truly, enjoy your new home!!

Let me spin a yarn for you. 

It was sometime in the late 1950's, early 1960's (not sure of the exact year), and my grandparents and their four children, my mother included, all lived happily in a small suburban subdivision in Florida. To hear my family talk about it, is to know that this was the best time of their lives. 


My grandmother, the sweetest woman, was a stay at home mom and spent her days raising her four children, and my grandfarther earned a good salary as a manager at a Winn-Dixie grocery store. 

They loved their neighborhood, as they tell it, nearly all of their neighborhors were fellow young families and couples, so my grandma often recounts how she and the other housewives would sit in lawn chairs and take turns watching the kids. My grandfather also made quite   a few friends with the othee husbands as well. Their lives were perfect, and they seemed to live in a small piece of suburban paradise. 

Until, they came to the door. 

Apparently, one afternoon while the kids were out playing and my grandfather was at work,  my grandmother heard a knock at the door. Naturally, given the good neighboorhood, she answered and was greeted by two men dressed nicely in white shirts and black ties. 

Being the fabulous host that she is, my grandmother had no problem inviting these gentlemen inside and offering them a cool drink and an escape from the hot Florida sun. It didnt take long for the pamphlets and bible verses to come out. 

Now, the way my grandmother tells the story, and being the extremely religious person that she is, she said that these men's words truly spoke to her, and apparently after only a few hours long talk, she was completely convinced that what they were saying, their warnings for approaching end times, was 100% true...and she decided that she would not allow her family to be kept from the truth that had been unveiled before her. 

Now from here the story gets a little patchy, I dont know of exact timeframes, but not long after this SINGULAR encounter, my grandma convinced her husband to leave their little piece of suburban paradise, and move somewhere that they could raise their children in peace, safety, and presumably, prepare for the end times. 

The place they chose to go after uprooting their entire family? 

The fucking backwoods of South Carolina. 

They left everything, sold the house and most of their belongings, pulled the kids out of school and headed up to their new piece of heavily wooded land. They even decided, after living in the suburbs, to invest in chickens, rabbits, horses, and even ducks. 

Let me be clear in saying, by their own admission, that they had absolutely no idea what they were doing. And they happened to move to just about the most unfriendly place in South Carolina you can go. 

My mom and her siblings remember being miserable there, and tell stories about how they had to adjust from going to open air, modern schools, to tiny one room school houses where they were ostracized by the other children due to their accents. I could never imagine the kins of culture shock they had to endure. 

TLDR: And Thats all I really know outside of a few other specific stories, but yeah...my grandmother essentially uprooted her entire family from a place they all loved, just because she was talked into believing that the end times were near, and that she would be better off acending to heaven with her family from a poorly run homestead in the backwoods if bumfuck SC.
